clue.text: Stay to see team following on

indicators.note: tells us the team word comes after the word for on in the answer

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter's subject line
a side is a team in a match

explanation.surface: A coach asks someone to stay behind and watch the team play on.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live or stay there, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bank holding little cash of late

indicators.note: says the word for bank contains the coin

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A bank has been sitting on a small amount of money lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to depend.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently and of late both mean in the recent past.

clue.text: Rough cut used in 'Home of the Stars'

indicators.note: says the cutting word goes inside the word for the stars' home

parts.note: the sky is where the stars are
to etch is to cut lines into a surface

explanation.surface: A rough edit of a film was used in a show about celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities; it means the ones in the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketchy plan is rough, incomplete and lacking detail.

clue.text: Clothed in idiosyncratic style hosting a new series of events

indicators.note: says the rearranged letters take the article inside them
an idiosyncratic style is quirky, so these letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone dressed eccentrically hosts a fresh sequence of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in idiosyncratic style' rearranges CLOTHED into DECTHLO; 'hosting' puts A inside it, then N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is an athletics contest made up of ten separate events.

clue.text: Muscles stretch — it's a kind of art

parts.note: abs are the abdominal muscles
a tract is a stretch of land

explanation.surface: A gallery-goer jokes that a painting of straining muscles counts as art.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract art is a non-representational style, one kind of art among many.

clue.text: After knock, taps turn each way

indicators.note: puts the taps after the word for knock

parts.note: a blow is a knock or hit
a basin's two taps are the hot and cold

explanation.surface: A plumber bangs the pipes, then turns each tap in both directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn each way' wants to be about taps; it means vacillate.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow hot and cold is to keep changing one's mind, swinging one way then the other.

clue.text: Work out sequence

definitions.meaning: a ... is a sequence, as in a ... of thought or events

explanation.definitionFit: Train covers both physical exercise and a connected series of things.

clue.text: Not recalling names, confused, I start to ad-lib

indicators.note: says the letters of the words are mixed up
says only the opening letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: An actor who can't remember names gets flustered and begins to improvise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges NAMES into AMNES; then I, and A starts ad-lib.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the state of not recalling things.

clue.text: Part of bible story, 'In the beginning', offering strength

indicators.note: places the story word at the start, ahead of the Bible part

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A Bible story that begins 'In the beginning' offers strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the beginning' looks like a quotation from Genesis; it says where the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural gift or strength; the Parable of the Talents is in the New Testament.

clue.text: Marks given for literary speeches

parts.note: sounds like grades awarded for oratory, but describes the punctuation marks placed round spoken words in written text

explanation.surface: Marks awarded for literary speeches in a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks' looks like scores; it means punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks surround dialogue in fiction, marking out what characters say.

clue.text: Endless street party — turn up the volume!

indicators.note: says the word for street loses its final letter

parts.note: a crescent is a curved street
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A street party that never ends, with someone shouting to crank the music up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims CRESCENT to CRESCEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Crescendo is the musical direction to grow gradually louder, an instruction to raise the volume.

clue.text: Cancel regular publication after second article is rejected

indicators.note: means that article is thrown out of the publication word

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
the indefinite article a, the second one in the word for the publication

explanation.surface: A magazine is cancelled after a second piece is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the second A from ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to cancel it or declare it void.

clue.text: After one gets tight, it goes all down one's shirt front

definitions.text: After one gets tight, it goes all down one's shirt front

parts.words: After one gets tight, it goes all down one's shirt front
parts.note: sounds like a drunk spilling drink down a shirt, but describes a knotted neckwear item, pulled tight at the collar, hanging down the shirt front

explanation.surface: A drunk spills drink all down the front of his shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' suggests drunk; here it is the knot being pulled tight at the collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is knotted tight at the collar and hangs down the length of a shirt front.

clue.text: Fully involved in Smith & Sons, taking part

indicators.note: says only part of the firm's name is taken, with the ampersand read as the word and

explanation.surface: A family firm of smiths where everyone is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Read '&' as AND: smitH AND SONs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on person is personally and practically involved rather than managing at a distance.

clue.text: Like his subjects, he hopes, sovereign needs new direction initially

indicators.note: says the first letter, the direction right, is swapped for another direction, left

parts.note: royal as a noun, a member of the ruling family

explanation.surface: A monarch hopes his people remain faithful while he seeks a fresh course.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) at the start of ROYAL becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch hopes subjects are faithful and true to the crown.

clue.text: Experiment bringing in uniform to class

indicators.note: says the word for experiment takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a trial is a test or experiment
U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A school trial brings in uniforms for a class.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a small teaching session, a kind of class.

clue.text: Artist bathing, showing result of a fall

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
someone bathing is in water

explanation.surface: An artist bathing shows the effect of a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' suggests a tumble; it is rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainwater is what accumulates after a fall of rain.

clue.text: Beads stolen, something tennis player sneaked in

parts.note: beads of liquid are drops
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Stolen beads smuggled in by a tennis player.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop shot is a soft stroke that barely clears the net, a sneaky winner in tennis.

clue.text: Attacked when excited

definitions.meaning: to have ... someone is to have attacked them suddenly

explanation.surface: Someone was attacked when they got worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both a sudden assault and being aroused or thrilled.

clue.text: University broadcast silent instrument

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A university broadcasts an instrument that makes no sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges SILENT into TENSIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, especially one used in a kitchen.

clue.text: Station underground with no opening in cold period

indicators.note: says the word for the cold season loses its first letter

parts.note: winter is the cold season

explanation.surface: A Tube station shut and without an entrance through the cold months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' is a verb: to place. 'Station underground' wants to be a Tube stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, placing a body in the ground.

clue.text: Gent's clothing classic, being dressed down

indicators.note: says the gent's word wraps round the other

parts.note: a toff is an upper-class gentleman; the 's is 'is'
old as in an old classic

explanation.surface: A gent's classic clothing, worn in a casually dressed-down way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed down' suggests casual wear; here it means scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: To be told off or dressed down is to be reprimanded.

clue.text: Chart mapping out twelve houses

parts.note: sounds like an estate plan, but the twelve houses are the astrological divisions of the sky

explanation.surface: A map showing a dozen homes on a street.
explanation.walkthrough: In astrology the sky is split into twelve 'houses', each tied to a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac is the band of twelve star signs used in astrological charts.

clue.text: Venison: age, roast while turning, infused with herb

indicators.note: says the letters found are read backwards
says the answer's letters are steeped within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A recipe: hang venison, roast it on a turning spit, and infuse with herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: venisON AGE ROast holds ONAGERO; 'while turning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a Mediterranean culinary herb, often paired with roast meats.

clue.text: Maybe ring with a time to come over

indicators.note: says the letters are flipped over, read backwards

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article before a vowel
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Perhaps a ring will come along with time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come over' reverses ANERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing ring or circus ring is a kind of arena, an enclosed space for contests.

clue.text: Plant making whiskey and lager retired by company

parts.note: W is Whiskey in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: here means the word for lager goes back, read in reverse

parts.note: pils is a pale lager, short for pilsner

explanation.surface: Someone makes whiskey and lager, then the firm withdraws the lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns PILS into SLIP; 'by company' places CO beside the rest, at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow-flowered wild primula of meadows.

clue.text: Take to court after one's dispute

indicators.note: puts the legal action after the word for one's

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals, plus the 's
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Someone goes to law over a personal quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter in dispute, as in 'take issue with' or 'the issue at stake'.

clue.text: Nipper that's going to shed at about six

definitions.text: Nipper that's going to shed at about six

parts.words: Nipper that's going to shed at about six
parts.note: a nipper is a child but also something that nips or bites; a child's first teeth start falling out at about age six

explanation.surface: A child that will be dropped off at a shed at around six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nipper' reads as a child; it is a biter. 'six' is an age, not a time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby teeth are the first set, which fall out from around age six.

clue.text: Boarding schoolmate's pal located around ruin

indicators.note: says the letters found are turned round, read backwards
means getting on board within the clue words, so the letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: A boarding-school friend's pal has been tracked down.
explanation.walkthrough: schoolmatE'S PAL LOCated holds ESPALLOC; 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to fall apart or be ruined, as a business or scheme can.

clue.text: Professor prepared to share female's earnings

indicators.note: says the female letter is shared by the two words, written only once

parts.note: fit means ready or prepared
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A professor ready to split a woman's income.
explanation.walkthrough: PROF and FIT overlap on their shared F, so it appears once.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is money gained, the earnings left after costs.
